Ghent had been grey for a week, and Selin's grandmother Elif was in bed at home in Izmir with a bad cough that would not lift. Selin's texts to her went unread, since the small letters made Elif tired. So Selin sat on the dorm bench near the bike racks and pressed record instead.
"Anneanne, it is me. It is raining here again, and the bakery on my street smells of your cinnamon buns, I almost cried. Drink your tea. I will call on Sunday and you can tell me about the neighbours."
Two hours later a voice note came back, crackly and warm: "My little one, I played yours three times."

qa.q: Where was Selin's grandmother Elif in bed?
qa.a: Elif was in bed at home in Izmir.

qa.q: What was Selin feeling while recording the note about the bakery?
qa.a: Selin felt homesick and tender toward Elif. Almost crying over the cinnamon buns that smell like the grandmother's shows how much Selin missed home.

qa.q: Why did Selin choose a voice note over another text, and what did it lead to?
qa.a: The small letters made Elif tired and Selin's texts went unread, so Selin recorded a voice note. Elif played it three times and answered in a warm voice of her own.

qa.q: What might Elif have felt when hearing Selin's voice on the recording?
qa.a: Elif probably felt comforted and loved, since a bad cough and a quiet room were replaced by Selin's voice. Playing the note three times shows how much it meant. 🤍

grounding: A young adult sends a voice note to an ill grandmother far away, and the warmth of the voice comforts more than a text could.

qa.q: What did Chetan do that helped Dadi and Simran understand each other?
qa.a: Chetan spoke Hindi to Dadi and English to Simran, and passed on what each said. That way neither of them was left out.

qa.q: What might Simran have felt when Dadi gave her a ladoo?
qa.a: Simran probably felt welcomed and a little curious, since Dadi's Hindi was new to her. The ladoo showed kindness without needing words.

grounding: A child speaks Hindi with Dadi and English with a friend, sensing which fits where.
